correctness.rationale: Each unoriented heptagon chord has normal angle j*pi/7 mod pi, yielding precisely 14 directed support normals, alternately support heights 1 and cos(pi/7). Sliding any feasible side to support never increases area; fewer-than-four side enclosures can be tightened by an additional allowed supporting line. Four normals in cyclic order yield a bounded intersection exactly when all four positive circular index gaps are <7. Four supporting halfplanes touch the heptagon, so edge lengths are nonnegative (possibly zero) and the exact shoelace/support formula A=sum[h_i h_next-(h_i²+h_next²)cos(g*pi/7)/2]/sin(g*pi/7) applies. There are 511 bounded quartets. The source interval certificate tests all 511 with 65-digit outward enclosures, 7 odd-index winners with gaps (2,4,4,4) and 504 strict losers, lower gap >0.025947319986; independent full high-precision enumeration of all 511 and optimizer reconstruction agreed. Exact winner area cos²(pi/7)[tan(pi/7)+3tan(2pi/7)] and ratio 1.258803773547..., equality exactly seven rotations. The finite exhaustive certificate is valid because geometric reduction proves no omitted continuum cases; high precision independent check alone is corroborative, not a substitute for rigorous interval certification.
